intro: A class (collar) is assigned before a run and changes a cat's stats and the abilities it can learn. After finishing a zone, talk to Butch to get the next class. Tiers are Greenside's personal ranking, not a rule; the Crap Guide author stresses that any class can work.

statRules.rule: 3 max mana per point, and some mana at the start of battle.
Mana gained at the end of each turn. A cat with 5 in every stat has 20 HP, 15 max mana and gains 5 mana a turn.
Melee classes (Fighter, Cleric, Tank, Butcher) scale their basic attack damage with it.
Ranged basic attack = base damage + (DEX - 5) / 2. A Hunter with 9 DEX does 6.
+2% crit chance on physical attacks per point. It also affects events, level-up options and every chance-based stat.
Movement and turn order. Above about 10-12 it has diminishing returns.
Everything except Strength, Dexterity and Luck. 4 CON (16 HP) survives two 10-damage hits; 8 CON (32 HP) survives four. Above 8 CON, spend points on damage.

classes.name: Fighter
classes.summary: The simplest melee class and the most durable damage dealer. Some abilities like low Intelligence, but the good ones cost 6-8 mana.
classes.pick: High HP, high INT, low speed, high luck.

classes.name: Hunter
classes.summary: Attacks, familiars and traps. Great damage and utility from range; the cost is fragility, a minimum range and low speed.
classes.pick: High DEX, high HP and high speed (best Hunter material).

classes.name: Mage
classes.summary: Hardest-hitting spells in the game, area damage and stuns. Range is only 3 tiles and needs line of sight, so Mages have to get close.
classes.pick: High DEX, high HP, middling speed, low CHA and luck.

classes.name: Tank
classes.summary: More a controller than a wall: almost every ability, including the basic attack, moves enemies. Pet rocks act as familiars. Goad pulls enemies in.
classes.pick: High STR, low HP, low INT, low to middling speed and luck. 7 STR lets them one-shot enemies with 8 HP or less via knockback.
classes.conflict: The Crap Guide gives -1 DEX -1 INT instead of -1 SPD -1 DEX.

classes.name: Cleric
classes.unlock: Reach the Sewers for the first time
classes.summary: The healer. Strong with armour on overheal, resurrects and damage from healing, but it needs good stats and synergy. Stopping enemies hurts more than healing back.
classes.pick: High STR, low HP, high INT, high speed, low luck.
classes.conflict: Greenside says Complete the Alley instead.

classes.name: Thief
classes.summary: The most mobile class. Big single-target damage through status effects and crits, and coins from pickups. Must be kept from being one-shot.
classes.pick: High DEX, high HP, low speed, high luck.

classes.name: Necromancer
classes.summary: Corpses, zombies and leeches. Its basic attack drains life, so it is the best ranged tank. A few abilities only work while downed.
classes.pick: High DEX, low HP, high speed, high INT, middling luck.

classes.name: Druid
classes.special: Permanent crow familiar that shares its stats
classes.summary: Its basic attack does no damage; the crow does. Summons, songs and forms. Songs work best at the start of a fight, so it wants speed. Summons are controllable (the Hunter's are not).
classes.pick: High STR, high HP, high INT and high speed (the cat that has everything).

classes.name: Tinkerer
classes.summary: No basic attack: it makes a weapon and throws it for 5 damage that scales with DEX. Hit-or-miss, but anything that gives tech is strong, and guns can kill a normal enemy each turn.
classes.pick: High DEX, high HP, high CHA, low INT. Low INT is fine: INT without CHA only wastes mana.

classes.name: Butcher
classes.special: No weapons; starts with a meat hook
classes.summary: Like a slow Fighter. The hook pulls units from any distance in 8 directions and basic attacks cleave out meat that heals. Fire cooks meat for double healing.
classes.pick: High STR, low HP, low to middling INT, high speed, high luck.

classes.name: Psychic
classes.summary: The controller: status effects and forced movement, many abilities with infinite range limited only by line of sight, and turn-order tricks. Damage scales with neither STR nor DEX.
classes.pick: Low STR and low DEX, especially with high HP. Keep it at the back, like a magic Hunter.

classes.name: Monk
classes.special: No weapons, trinkets or healing items; attacks twice per turn
classes.summary: Switches between melee and a lobbed ranged attack with the built-in Stance Switcher, and likes having little equipment, so it suits budget runs.
classes.pick: High STR and high DEX, or a cat with mutations that help both range and melee.
classes.conflict: The Crap Guide gives +2 CHA instead of +1.

classes.name: Jester
classes.summary: Gets random abilities from every other class and a few very strong ones of its own. Very strong or very weak depending on luck, like Eden in Isaac.

classes.name: Collarless
classes.summary: By design the weakest class: weak, situational and overpriced abilities, and no stat bonus. It can pick skills from other classes on level-up, so it needs a good base attack.
classes.pick: Balanced stats with high STR and a melee attack, or high DEX and a ranged one.

sides: How to Unlock all Classes: reach the Sewers for the first time.
Greenside: complete the Alley. (That is the same step, since finishing the Alley opens the Sewers.)
How to Unlock all Classes: +4 CON, -1 SPD, -1 DEX.
A Crap Guide To Classes: +4 CON, -1 DEX, -1 INT.
How to Unlock all Classes: +2 INT, +1 CHA, -1 STR, -1 DEX.
A Crap Guide To Classes: +2 INT, +2 CHA, -1 STR, -1 DEX.
Greenside: B tier (it used to be A). Early Game Tips and the Reddit post say it is the weakest starter.
Crap Guide: it hits harder than any other class, including what it calls the strongest spell in the game, Meteor Storm.
discrepancies.verdict: Strong with the right spells and stats; it needs more setup than Hunter, Tank or Cleric.
